segments.text: Are they cheating, or is it just normal variation? Hypothesis testing decides.
segments.caption: Are they cheating, or is it just normal variation? Hypothesis testing decides.

segments.text: Here's the textbook definition, the one to use in interviews.
segments.caption: Here's the textbook definition, the one to use in interviews.

segments.text: Hypothesis testing is a statistical method that uses sample data to decide between two competing claims about a population: the null hypothesis and the alternative hypothesis.
segments.caption: Hypothesis testing is a statistical method that uses sample data to decide between two competing claims about a population: the null hypothesis and the alternative hypothesis.

segments.text: In plain words: is the pattern in the data real, or just chance?
segments.caption: In plain words: is the pattern in the data real, or just chance?

segments.text: The null hypothesis, H zero, says nothing special is going on: the packets really average fifty grams.
segments.caption: The null hypothesis, H0, says nothing special is going on: the packets really average 50 grams.

segments.text: The alternative, H one, says something is going on: they average less.
segments.caption: The alternative, H1, says something is going on: they average less.

segments.text: We always start by assuming the null is true.
segments.caption: We always start by assuming the null is true.

segments.text: Every test has this pair.
segments.caption: Every test has this pair.

segments.text: A coin: fair, or biased. A website button: no change, or more clicks.
segments.caption: A coin: fair, or biased. A website button: no change, or more clicks.

segments.text: A new teaching method: no difference, or higher scores.

segments.text: It's like a courtroom: innocent until proven guilty.
segments.caption: It's like a courtroom: innocent until proven guilty.

segments.text: We reject the null only with strong evidence. Not enough evidence means not guilty, which is not the same as innocent.
segments.caption: We reject the null only with strong evidence. Not enough evidence means not guilty, which is not the same as innocent.

segments.text: A test has four steps.
segments.caption: A test has four steps.

segments.text: One: state the two hypotheses. Two: pick a significance level, usually five percent.
segments.caption: One: state the two hypotheses. Two: pick a significance level, usually 5%.

segments.text: Three: calculate the p-value.
segments.caption: Three: calculate the p-value.

segments.text: If the packets really averaged fifty grams, an average this low would happen only about one percent of the time.
segments.caption: If the packets really averaged 50 grams, an average this low would happen only about 1% of the time.

segments.text: Four: decide. One percent is below five percent, so we reject the null. The packets really are underfilled.
segments.caption: Four: decide. 1% is below 5%, so we reject the null. The packets really are underfilled.

segments.text: Now suppose the average had been forty-nine and a half grams.
segments.caption: Now suppose the average had been 49.5 grams.

segments.text: That happens about twenty-seven percent of the time by chance, so we fail to reject the null.
segments.caption: That happens about 27% of the time by chance, so we fail to reject the null.

segments.text: That doesn't prove the packets are full. There's just not enough evidence.
segments.caption: That doesn't prove the packets are full. There's just not enough evidence.

segments.text: One more example: a coin lands heads nine times out of ten.
segments.caption: One more example: a coin lands heads 9 times out of 10.

segments.text: If the coin were fair, nine or more heads would happen only about one percent of the time.
segments.caption: If the coin were fair, 9 or more heads would happen only about 1% of the time.

segments.text: Below five percent, so we reject the null. The coin is probably biased.
